record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: Describe the kneading set K of the Lozi map, that is, characterize all kneading sequences that occur.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. — Describe the set of kneading sequences K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real parameters $a,b$ with $b\neq 0$, the Lozi map $L_{a,b}\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ is defined by
$$L_{a,b}(x,y) \;=\; \bigl(1 + y - a|x|,\; b\,x\bigr).$$
For parameters in the classical region where $L_{a,b}$ admits a strange attractor $\Lambda$ (e.g. $0<b<1$ and $a$ such that $L_{a,b}$ is hyperbolic with a transitive attractor), associate to each point $p\in\Lambda$ its symbolic itinerary $(s_n(p))_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ defined by $s_n(p)=\mathrm{sgn}(\pi_1(L_{a,b}^{\,n}(p)))$, where $\pi_1$ denotes the first coordinate (with appropriate convention on the singular line $\{x=0\}$). The kneading set $K=K(a,b)$ is defined as the collection of itineraries (or, equivalently, of forward itineraries of images of the critical line $\{x=0\}$ under iteration) that arise in this way.

Problem. Give an intrinsic combinatorial characterization of the kneading set $K$ of the Lozi map: describe exactly which sequences in $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ (resp. $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$) occur as kneading sequences, in a manner analogous to the Milnor–Thurston admissibility characterization for kneading sequences of unimodal interval maps.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are available: Misiurewicz and Štimac (2016, "Symbolic dynamics for Lozi maps", and subsequent works on Lozi-like maps and folding patterns) have characterized the set of itineraries of points in the Lozi attractor via the kneading set, showing that there are countably many kneading sequences and introducing the equivalent folding pattern/folding tree encoding. Related work (Markov partitions, Lyapunov exponents) has built on this. However, a fully intrinsic admissibility characterization of K analogous to Milnor–Thurston for unimodal maps does not yet appear to be settled in full generality, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Symbolic dynamics for Lozi maps
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces kneading sequences for the Lozi map and characterizes the set of itineraries of points in the Lozi attractor.
status_evidence.claim: A characterization of itineraries via kneading sequences exists, with countably many kneading sequences.

status_evidence.title: Lozi-like maps
status_evidence.snippet: Folding pattern and folding tree are introduced as equivalent encodings of the kneading set for Lozi-like maps.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalent combinatorial encodings (folding pattern/tree) of the kneading set have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Markov partition in the attractor of Lozi maps
status_evidence.snippet: Uses kneading theory to define Markov partitions for Lozi attractors.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work uses but does not complete an intrinsic Milnor–Thurston-type characterization.
